one_sentence_story: In 2009, volunteers lying inside a cramped, noisy brain scanner were asked to tell the next patient the scanner was pleasant — and the harder their brain's conflict alarm and gut-discomfort center fired during the white lie, the more they genuinely convinced themselves they liked the scanner.
so_what_for_you: Whenever you choose to say or do something you don't really believe without an obvious outside excuse, your brain's error alarm hates the mismatch so much that it quietly rewrites your real opinion to match what you said.

jargon_map.plain: mental friction when your actions clash with your real beliefs
jargon_map.analogy: like interlocking relay dials grinding until one side gives way
like a red dashboard warning light when steering and wheels point opposite ways
like the uneasy knot in your stomach during an awkward fib

jargon_map.plain: politely getting someone to argue against their own view by 'free choice'
jargon_map.analogy: like asking a tired camper to record a sunny camp commercial

jargon_map.plain: an outside excuse like extra pay that explains away the fib
jargon_map.analogy: like an actor reading a commercial script for a paycheck without believing it

jargon_map.plain: genuinely updating your own rating so the inner clash disappears
jargon_map.analogy: like deciding you actually love bitter coffee because you bought the big bag
